sections.h2: Does Maine have an estate tax or an inheritance tax?
sections.html:
Maine has an estate tax, not an inheritance tax. The tax is figured on the whole estate before it is distributed, and heirs do not owe a separate tax on what they receive. One legal publisher's overview notes that the state does not impose an inheritance tax and that the estate tax fully replaced it for deaths after June 30, 1986.

For a family holding a house, the useful question is whether the estate is large enough to owe anything, and whether the paperwork for the lien release is in order. Most Maine estates owe no estate tax, yet many still have to file a short form so the house can be sold with a clean title.

The state's own definitions sit in 36 M.R.S. §4102. It treats the "adjusted federal gross estate" as the federal gross estate adjusted for Maine elective property, plus taxable gifts made in the year before death. A "resident" is a person domiciled in Maine at death, and a "nonresident" is someone domiciled elsewhere.

sections.h2: What is the Maine estate tax exclusion for 2026?
sections.html:
The 2026 Maine exclusion amount is $7,160,000. Maine Revenue Services publishes the amount for each year, and it has moved up over time.

Year of deathMaine exclusion amount
2023$6,410,000
2024$6,800,000
2025$7,000,000
2026$7,160,000

The federal exclusion for 2026 decedents is $15,000,000, according to the 2026 Form 706ME instructions. That gap is why a Maine estate can owe state tax even when no federal return is needed.

sections.h2: What are the Maine estate tax rates?
sections.html:
Tax applies only to the amount above the exclusion, in three steps. Table A in the 2026 Form 706ME instructions sets the rates.

Maine taxable amount (line 5)Tax
$7,160,000 or less$0
Over $7,160,000 up to $10,160,0008% of the amount over $7,160,000
Over $10,160,000 up to $13,160,000$240,000 plus 10% of the amount over $10,160,000
Over $13,160,000$540,000 plus 12% of the amount over $13,160,000

Interest and penalties are added to the tax owed. They are not deductions on the return.

sections.h2: Who has to file a Maine estate tax return?
sections.html:
A Maine return is required when the estate is above the threshold or when a federal estate tax return is required. The state lists the filing tests in its FAQ and the Form 706ME instructions.

  • A federal estate tax return is required.
  • The federal gross estate plus taxable gifts made within one year of death plus Maine elective property exceeds the threshold.
  • The Maine QTIP election on line 2 of Form 706ME is greater than zero.

Form 706ME applies to Maine residents, and to nonresidents who owned Maine real or tangible personal property at death. If a nonresident held Maine land through a trust, LLC or other pass-through entity, the state may still treat it as Maine property unless the entity had a valid business purpose, carried on a for-profit business and was acquired in a bona fide sale for full consideration. The personal representative files. If no one has been appointed, a person in possession of the estate's property is treated as the representative.

sections.h2: When is the return due, and can the estate get more time?
sections.html:
The return is due nine months after the date of death. Maine gives an automatic extension to file equal to any federal extension or six months, whichever is longer.

  • An extension to file does not extend the time to pay. Tax is due by the original date, and interest runs on unpaid tax.
  • A longer extension request must be in writing before the automatic six-month period ends, and the total generally cannot exceed eight months.
  • Estates largely made up of closely held business interests may request a payment extension under 36 M.R.S. §4109.
  • Penalties may be waived for reasonable cause. Interest waivers are rare.

Forms and payments go through the Maine Tax Portal, which does not require an account for estate tax filings. Form 706ME must be filed and paid electronically.

sections.h2: What is the Maine estate tax lien, and how does it affect a house sale?
sections.html:
Maine law places an automatic lien on a decedent's Maine real and tangible personal property at death. A buyer's title company will want to see a release before it insures a purchase, so the lien matters whenever an estate sells a house.

The representative requests the release with a Certificate of Discharge of Estate Tax Lien, plus either Form 706ME or Form 700-SOV (Statement of Value) and any required proof of value. The 706ME instructions cite 36 M.R.S. §4112 for the lien. The State Tax Assessor signs the certificate and mails it back, and the original is recorded with the county Registry of Deeds.

  • If no return is otherwise required, the estate files Form 700-SOV with the certificate to request the release.
  • Probate courts may require Form 700-SOV or 706ME even when no tax is owed.
  • If you lack the deed's book and page, the Registry of Deeds can help you find the reference.

Maine has 17 registry of deeds offices, one for each county and two for Aroostook, so the certificate must go to the office where the house sits.

sections.h2: How should heirs plan a sale around the lien and the tax?
sections.html:
Start the paperwork early, because the release is often the step that sets the closing date. Even a small estate with a single house benefits from a clear timeline.

  1. Confirm the date of death and value of all assets to see whether the estate is near the $7,160,000 threshold.
  2. Get a date-of-death appraisal of the house. The same value is generally used for the heirs' basis under IRS Publication 551.
  3. Prepare Form 700-SOV or Form 706ME with the Certificate of Discharge.
  4. Submit electronically through the Maine Tax Portal and wait for the signed certificate.
  5. Record the original at the registry of deeds in the county where the house is located.
  6. Schedule the closing after the release is recorded.

Maine also has other probate steps that run in parallel, covered in our Maine probate guide. A personal representative needs authority from the probate court to sign a deed, so line up those letters at the same time.

sections.h2: How do cash buyers handle an estate sale in Maine?
sections.html:
A cash buyer can close without bank underwriting, but the lien release and the estate's authority still decide the timeline. Heirs often come to us with a house that needs repairs, or one that sits empty while a family decides what to do. We buy as-is, and we work with your attorney or personal representative on the documents the title company needs.

This page is general information. For a specific estate, check with the personal representative's attorney or Maine Revenue Services before you sign a purchase contract.

faqs.q: What is the Maine estate tax threshold in 2026?
faqs.a: $7,160,000. Estates below that generally owe no Maine estate tax, though a form may still be needed to release the lien on real estate. The amount was $7,000,000 for 2025 and $6,800,000 for 2024.

faqs.q: Does Maine have an inheritance tax?
faqs.a: No. Maine uses an estate tax only, which is figured on the estate rather than on each heir's share. One published overview says the estate tax fully replaced the old inheritance tax for deaths after June 30, 1986.

faqs.q: Can heirs sell an inherited house in Maine before the estate tax is paid?
faqs.a: Usually the title company will require the Certificate of Discharge of Estate Tax Lien first. The lien attaches automatically at death, and the release is recorded at the county registry of deeds. Ask the personal representative's attorney how to time it.

It is the Statement of Value, which an estate files with a certificate request to release the lien when no estate tax return is otherwise required. The state says probate courts may ask for it even when no tax is owed.

faqs.q: When is the Maine estate tax return due?
faqs.a: Nine months after the date of death. Maine allows an automatic filing extension of six months or the federal extension, whichever is longer, but payment is still due by the original date.

faqs.q: Does a nonresident who owns a Maine house have to file?
faqs.a: Often yes. Form 706ME applies to nonresidents who owned Maine real or tangible personal property at death, and the estate's Maine property is entered on line 6a. The same lien release process applies.
